headline: Iran-linked hackers push their water-system attacks past Minnesota into at least six more states as actively exploited flaws in N-able and SonicWall gear hand intruders enterprise networks.

emerging_trends.text: Iran-linked hackers have pushed their water-system intrusions past Minnesota into at least six more states, underscoring how thinly defended municipal utilities have become the front line of geopolitical conflict.
emerging_trends.topic_title: US Water Attacks Spread to Six More States

emerging_trends.text: Attackers are racing through freshly disclosed flaws in remote-management and access gear, seizing N-able's N-central servers after an incomplete fix while INC ransomware roots SonicWall SMA1000 appliances.
emerging_trends.topic_title: N-able N-central Servers Seized via CVE-2026-18577

emerging_trends.text: Malicious model repositories now run arbitrary code through Hugging Face's Diffusers library, extending the software supply-chain threat squarely into the AI ecosystem.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Hugging Face Diffusers Flaws Enable Code Execution

topics.title: US Water Attacks Spread to Six More States
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported the Iran-linked campaign now reaches water systems in at least six more states, including Michigan, South Dakota, and Georgia, beyond the Minnesota utilities first tied to Tehran.
topics.summary: Iran-linked hackers target internet-exposed programmable logic controllers across US water and wastewater systems; CISA urges operators to pull the exposed devices offline immediately.

sources.title: US Water Cyberattacks Extend Beyond Minnesota to at Least 6 Other States

topics.title: N-able N-central Servers Seized via CVE-2026-18577
topics.latest_developments: N-able confirmed attackers exploited authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-18577 to gain remote administrative control of N-central servers after its first patch proved incomplete, shipping build 2026.3.1.7 on August 2 as the first unaffected version.
topics.summary: N-central is N-able's remote monitoring and management platform that managed service providers use to run customer fleets; the bypass lets intruders reach every system managed through a compromised server, so operators must upgrade to build 2026.3.1.7 now.

sources.title: N-able Says Attackers Take Over N-central Servers After Initial Fix Proves Incomplete

topics.title: Hugging Face Diffusers Flaws Enable Code Execution
topics.latest_developments: Researchers disclosed three high-severity flaws in Hugging Face's Diffusers library that let crafted model repositories run arbitrary code while bypassing the trust_remote_code safeguard.
topics.summary: The Diffusers library loads AI image and diffusion models; a malicious repository executes code on any machine that loads it, opening the AI supply chain to attack.

sources.title: Hugging Face Diffusers Flaws Could Let Model Repositories Execute Arbitrary Code

topics.title: INC Ransomware Roots SonicWall SMA1000 Appliances
topics.latest_developments: The INC Ransomware gang is exploiting recent SonicWall SMA1000 vulnerabilities to seize root access and move laterally, SecurityWeek reported.
topics.summary: SonicWall's SMA1000 secure-access appliances sit at network edges; INC Ransomware uses the flaws to gain root and spread, so administrators should patch and hunt for signs of compromise.

sources.title: Recent SonicWall Vulnerabilities Exploited in Ransomware Attacks

topics.title: Chinese Actor Deploys GHOSTBLADE on iOS
topics.latest_developments: Censys identified an unknown Chinese threat actor deploying the GHOSTBLADE implant on Apple iOS devices with a publicly leaked version of the DarkSword exploit kit, running more than 100 web properties.
topics.summary: The actor lures iOS users through fake Amazon Web Services sign-in pages hosted on a domain that also serves the DarkSword toolkit, most of the roughly 100 sites posing as AWS logins.

sources.title: Chinese Threat Actor Uses Leaked DarkSword Kit to Deploy GHOSTBLADE on iOS

topics.title: PNLD Breach Exposes UK Police Contacts
topics.latest_developments: The Police National Legal Database confirmed a breach identified July 26 that dumped names, organizations, and work email addresses of British police officers, staff, and criminal justice professionals onto the dark web.
topics.summary: PNLD supplies legal reference data to UK police forces and government partners; the leak exposes contact details of officers, criminal justice professionals, and customers.

sources.title: PNLD Breach Exposes U.K. Police and Government Contact Details on Dark Web

business_politics.title: U.S. and Japan Jointly Prop Up the Yen
business_politics.latest_developments: Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama and the U.S. Treasury confirmed the move was a coordinated U.S.-Japan intervention, the first since 1998, and both governments vowed to act again against disorderly currency swings.
business_politics.summary: The New York Fed bought yen alongside Japanese authorities after the currency touched a 40-year low against the dollar, the first coordinated U.S.-Japan intervention since 1998, an effort to contain the tremors a cratering yen could send through global markets.

sources.title: U.S., Japan Intervene to Boost Yen for First Time Since 1998
Japan vows further yen intervention with US if needed
